bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Government Policy Risk — The Company explicitly identifies Government Policy Risk as a key risk relating to policy revisions and subsidy-driven recoveries. As a fertilizer producer, realisations depend on the Nutrient-Based Subsidy regime and Department of Fertilizers supply objectives, so a change in subsidy rates or policy directly alters the economics of the fertilizer segment.
- Input Price Risk and raw material cost volatility — Listed by the Company as a key risk covering input and natural gas prices. During FY 2025-26, average CFR prices of phosphoric acid, ammonia, rock phosphate and sulphur surged, with sulphur recording a steep rise, placing pressure on industry margins; the fertilizer business environment became increasingly challenging in the fourth quarter as a result.
- Raw Material Availability Risk — Identified by the Company as a key risk. Escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East towards the close of FY 2025-26 disrupted energy and commodity supply chains and the availability of critical feedstocks including natural gas, ammonia and sulphur, particularly during March 2026. Scheduled maintenance shutdowns at major Middle East ammonia facilities reduced global availability.
- Phosphatic Fertilizer Market Risk — Named by the Company as a key risk relating to domestic phosphatic fertilizer prices. The Company mitigates it by focusing on production of various complex grade fertilizers at Sikka and targeted product/segment strategies to maximise sales while leveraging its existing portfolio.
- Market Condition Risk in Industrial Products — global chemical overcapacity and dumping — International prices declined by approximately 21% for Nylon-6 Chips, 20% for Caprolactam and 10% for Melamine, largely attributable to global overcapacity particularly in China, subdued demand and trade disruptions. The Caprolactam-Benzene spread remained under pressure for most of the year on subdued international realisations and the continued risk of dumping of Caprolactam and downstream products into India.
- Currency Risk — Explicitly identified by the Company as a key risk relating to foreign exchange fluctuations. Exposure arises from imported raw materials priced in USD (phosphoric acid, ammonia, rock phosphate, sulphur) and from a growing export book, and is managed through efficient Foreign Exchange Risk Management.
- Monsoon and weather dependence of agricultural demand — The demand outlook will remain influenced by the progress of the south-west monsoon and the possible emergence of El Nino conditions. Declining soil health, intensive cultivation and erratic weather patterns place greater pressure on farm economics, and downstream demand for the fertilizer portfolio moves with these agricultural conditions.
- Vintage asset reliability and process safety exposure — The Company operates vintage plants requiring recurring refurbishment, including the Ammonium Sulphate-I and AS-II Plants and the Urea-II Plant revamp undertaken to improve reliability. R&D investigation identified Ammonia Stress Corrosion Cracking at weld heat-affected zones as the cause of recurring liquid ammonia pipeline leakages in the Urea-II plant, underlining process safety exposure at an integrated ammonia-handling complex.

outlook.body:
- A ten-year Growth Strategy Plan frames the next phase of expansion, bringing together business growth, process improvement, operational efficiency, asset optimisation and disciplined project prioritisation, and is designed to increase integration, diversification and value addition across the portfolio.
- Improve control over critical inputs through backward integration at Sikka via a 600 MTPD phosphoric acid plant and a 1,800 MTPD sulphuric acid plant, reducing dependence on externally sourced inputs and improving supply security.
- Move into higher-value applications by evaluating new chemical molecules, new business chains and ultra-pure and specialised applications, with potential applications identified in food, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and electric-vehicle battery value chains.
- Complement the bulk fertiliser portfolio with specialty and non-bulk fertilisers and crop-protection products, shaped around agro-climatic zones, cropping patterns and specific crop and soil needs, and introduce herbicide and insecticide offerings.
- Expand export markets across Africa, Europe, ASEAN and other Asian markets, particularly for industrial products and specialised fertilisers.
- Extract greater value from existing manufacturing, storage and logistics assets through better integration and utilisation, including third-party opportunities such as ammonia trading using Jamnagar ammonia-handling and storage infrastructure.
- Shift from relatively fixed pricing, procurement and product-mix decisions towards a dynamic assessment of market conditions and product economics, redirecting capacity and effort where returns justify it.
- Modify the C-Train facility at Sikka to provide flexibility between DAP and APS production so output can be aligned with market requirements and raw-material economics.
- Develop the proposed Dahej Complex on 276.70 hectares leased from GIDC, with preliminary product configuration evaluated against opportunities identified under the Growth Strategy Plan.
- Grow renewable energy use to reduce power costs and environmental footprint, building on an aggregate renewable capacity of 217.94 MW.
- Strengthen R&D and technology to build proprietary products, processes and applications, moving beyond established offerings.
- Deepen farmer engagement beyond product supply through extension, advisory, Krishijivan, the Drone Didi concept and digital initiatives, supported by GSFC Agrotech's retail network.
- Build the specialised talent pipeline through recruitment, structured succession planning for critical positions, internal mobility and continuous learning platforms such as e-Gurukul and the L3 programme.
- Under the Growth Strategy Plan up to 2035 and Vision 2047, effect a strategic shift towards chemicals while maintaining growth in fertilizers, with focus on specialty and bulk chemicals, specialty fertilizers and crop protection, and green chemicals including green hydrogen and green ammonia.

outlook.body: GSFC reported a set of projects under execution or executed during FY 2025-26. Commissioned during the year were a 15 MW (AC) ground-mounted solar power plant at Charanka, Gujarat in May 2025; a 600 MTPD Sulphuric Acid Plant (Sulphuric Acid-V) at the Vadodara Unit in January 2026, executed on LSTK basis by ISGEC Heavy Engineering Limited with DMCC technology; and the revamp of the existing Urea-II Plant in May 2025 to reduce energy consumption and improve reliability, with Casale SA, Switzerland as technology supplier and Larsen & Toubro Limited as EPC contractor. Refurbishment of the vintage Ammonium Sulphate-II Plant was largely completed in March 2025 with remaining shutdown-linked activities carried out in March 2026, while refurbishment of the Ammonium Sulphate-I Plant was completed in May 2026, both carried out in-house. Under a group-captive arrangement with GACL, GSFC participated in GIPCL's 75 MW solar power project by equity infusion, with 25 MW (Phase I) commissioned in April 2025 and the balance 50 MW (Phase II) in June 2025; on equal equity infusion GSFC receives the benefit of generation from 37.5 MW. Projects in progress include backward integration at the Sikka Unit through a proposed 600 MTPD Phosphoric Acid Plant (technology supplier TECI, Tunisia) and an 1,800 MTPD Sulphuric Acid Plant (technology supplier Chemetics, Canada), with Projects & Development India Limited engaged as Project Management Consultant; technology and project-management partners have been appointed, the EPC contractor appointment process has been initiated and the EPC contract is expected to be awarded by September 2026. The C-Train at Sikka, presently designed only for DAP, is being modified to produce APS or DAP on a swing basis with INCRO, Spain as technology supplier and engineering, procurement and construction carried out in-house; the project is expected to be commissioned in July 2026. For the proposed Dahej Complex, the Company executed a 99-year land lease deed with GIDC in November 2025 for a 276.7 hectare land parcel at Dahej, Gujarat, with preliminary product configuration under preparation integrating products suggested by the Growth Strategy Consultant and identified in-house. During FY 2025-26 Sikka C-Train and PA SA were among the projects under implementation, while additional projects progressed to advanced stages of approval for FY 2026-27.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Indian fertilizer industry is expected to be bolstered by favourable agricultural fundamentals, including greater crop sowing, consistent government policy support and steady fertilizer demand.
- Industry performance will be impacted by volatile raw material prices, geopolitical developments and global supply chain disruptions.
- The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has projected a total fertilizer requirement of 390.54 LMT for the upcoming kharif season.
- Announcement of Nutrient-Based Subsidy rates for H1 FY2026-27, including a 10% increase in Nitrogen, Phosphorus and Sulphur nutrient support, reflects government commitment to fertilizer availability during the upcoming Kharif season.
- The demand outlook will remain influenced by the progress of the south-west monsoon and the possible emergence of El Nino conditions; revival of rainfall during July 2026 has improved the outlook for the agri-input sector ahead of the Rabi season.
- Restoration of 100% natural gas supply enabled a significant increase in domestic fertilizer production.
- The Company will maintain a balanced approach towards optimising sales opportunities, strategic stock placements and margin management, while remaining closely aligned with Department of Fertilizers supply objectives.
- In the Industrial Products segment, global chemical prices declined on global overcapacity particularly in China, subdued demand and trade disruptions, with Nylon-6 Chips down approximately 21%, Caprolactam 20% and Melamine 10% year-on-year.
- The Caprolactam-Benzene spread remained under pressure for most of the year on subdued international Caprolactam realisations and the continued risk of dumping into India, but improved significantly during the fourth quarter.
- Domestic Melamine demand remained subdued on lower operating rates in downstream laminate and plywood industries, partly mitigated by a strategic focus on exports.
- Margin levers are a focused product strategy, optimized product mix, higher-realisation products and markets, higher Melamine exports, increased Technical Grade Urea and HX Crystal sales and higher traded ammonia volumes.
- The strategy envisages increasing the share of value-added chemicals and exports to approximately one-third of total revenues, leveraging long-term trade agreements and the global China+1 shift.
- Competitiveness is increasingly shaped by the ability to manage costs, maintain reliable supplies and adapt product offerings to changing demand.
- Chemical exports increased from approximately US$15 million in FY2024-25 to more than US$29 million in FY2025-26, opening new overseas markets.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: GSFC is a multi-product industrial public sector enterprise co-promoted by the Government of Gujarat, established in 1962 and headquartered in Vadodara, specialising in the manufacture and marketing of fertilizers and industrial chemicals.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: GSFC manufactures and markets fertilizers and industrial chemicals through two reportable segments. The Fertilizer segment covers urea, Ammonium Sulphate, Di-ammonium Phosphate, Ammonium Phosphate Sulphate and NPK grades sold to farmers, while the Industrial Products segment supplies caprolactam, nylon-6, melamine, technical grade urea and HX Crystal to engineering plastics, automobiles, packaging, textiles, laminates, paints, pharmaceuticals and agrochemical customers. Its integrated production structure links feedstocks, intermediates, co-products and finished products across the Vadodara and Sikka units, supported by wholly owned subsidiary GSFC Agrotech Limited's retail network.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The Indian fertilizer industry is expected to be bolstered by favourable agricultural fundamentals, including greater crop sowing, consistent government policy support and steady fertilizer demand.
- Industry performance will be impacted by volatile raw material prices, geopolitical developments and global supply chain disruptions.
- The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has projected a total fertilizer requirement of 390.54 LMT for the upcoming kharif season.
- Announcement of Nutrient-Based Subsidy rates for H1 FY2026-27, including a 10% increase in Nitrogen, Phosphorus and Sulphur nutrient support, reflects government commitment to fertilizer availability during the upcoming Kharif season.
- The demand outlook will remain influenced by the progress of the south-west monsoon and the possible emergence of El Nino conditions; revival of rainfall during July 2026 has improved the outlook for the agri-input sector ahead of the Rabi season.
- Restoration of 100% natural gas supply enabled a significant increase in domestic fertilizer production.
- The Company will maintain a balanced approach towards optimising sales opportunities, strategic stock placements and margin management, while remaining closely aligned with Department of Fertilizers supply objectives.
- In the Industrial Products segment, global chemical prices declined on global overcapacity particularly in China, subdued demand and trade disruptions, with Nylon-6 Chips down approximately 21%, Caprolactam 20% and Melamine 10% year-on-year.
- The Caprolactam-Benzene spread remained under pressure for most of the year on subdued international Caprolactam realisations and the continued risk of dumping into India, but improved significantly during the fourth quarter.
- Domestic Melamine demand remained subdued on lower operating rates in downstream laminate and plywood industries, partly mitigated by a strategic focus on exports.
- Margin levers are a focused product strategy, optimized product mix, higher-realisation products and markets, higher Melamine exports, increased Technical Grade Urea and HX Crystal sales and higher traded ammonia volumes.
- The strategy envisages increasing the share of value-added chemicals and exports to approximately one-third of total revenues, leveraging long-term trade agreements and the global China+1 shift.
- Competitiveness is increasingly shaped by the ability to manage costs, maintain reliable supplies and adapt product offerings to changing demand.
- Chemical exports increased from approximately US$15 million in FY2024-25 to more than US$29 million in FY2025-26, opening new overseas markets.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: GSFC reported a set of projects under execution or executed during FY 2025-26. Commissioned during the year were a 15 MW (AC) ground-mounted solar power plant at Charanka, Gujarat in May 2025; a 600 MTPD Sulphuric Acid Plant (Sulphuric Acid-V) at the Vadodara Unit in January 2026, executed on LSTK basis by ISGEC Heavy Engineering Limited with DMCC technology; and the revamp of the existing Urea-II Plant in May 2025 to reduce energy consumption and improve reliability, with Casale SA, Switzerland as technology supplier and Larsen & Toubro Limited as EPC contractor. Refurbishment of the vintage Ammonium Sulphate-II Plant was largely completed in March 2025 with remaining shutdown-linked activities carried out in March 2026, while refurbishment of the Ammonium Sulphate-I Plant was completed in May 2026, both carried out in-house. Under a group-captive arrangement with GACL, GSFC participated in GIPCL's 75 MW solar power project by equity infusion, with 25 MW (Phase I) commissioned in April 2025 and the balance 50 MW (Phase II) in June 2025; on equal equity infusion GSFC receives the benefit of generation from 37.5 MW. Projects in progress include backward integration at the Sikka Unit through a proposed 600 MTPD Phosphoric Acid Plant (technology supplier TECI, Tunisia) and an 1,800 MTPD Sulphuric Acid Plant (technology supplier Chemetics, Canada), with Projects & Development India Limited engaged as Project Management Consultant; technology and project-management partners have been appointed, the EPC contractor appointment process has been initiated and the EPC contract is expected to be awarded by September 2026. The C-Train at Sikka, presently designed only for DAP, is being modified to produce APS or DAP on a swing basis with INCRO, Spain as technology supplier and engineering, procurement and construction carried out in-house; the project is expected to be commissioned in July 2026. For the proposed Dahej Complex, the Company executed a 99-year land lease deed with GIDC in November 2025 for a 276.7 hectare land parcel at Dahej, Gujarat, with preliminary product configuration under preparation integrating products suggested by the Growth Strategy Consultant and identified in-house. During FY 2025-26 Sikka C-Train and PA SA were among the projects under implementation, while additional projects progressed to advanced stages of approval for FY 2026-27.

themes.title: Fertilizer subsidy & nutrient-policy cycle
themes.need: Fertilizer makers are driven by NBS/urea subsidy policy, gas-pooling and nutrient pricing rather than the crop-protection volume/molecule-launch recovery. Q1FY27's supply-side read comes from MBAPL: revenue roughly flat at INR 416cr with EBITDA +16% and PAT +17% purely on cheap March-bought raw material that management said is now EXHAUSTED, with utilisation only ~43-45% because of raw-material availability rather than demand - SSP sales were +28% and NPK +33% YoY against production down 7%/28%. Its Dhule (Maharashtra) integrated complex commissions +3,30,000 MTPA DAP-NPK plus 99,000 MTPA phosphoric acid in Oct-2026 and a second phase in Oct-2027, framed as a >50% turnover jump toward ~INR 3,500cr revenue and 15.6 lakh MT capacity by FY28; Egypt/Jordan rock-phosphate sourcing (non-Hormuz) insulated it relative to import-dependent peers. Subsidy clarity and gas costs still set the near-term margin.
themes.driver: NBS/urea subsidy policy (the Oct-Mar rate revision), gas-pooling and nutrient pricing; MBAPL's Oct-2026 Dhule commissioning and the utilisation ramp toward ~90%; kharif demand pull-through after a delayed monsoon.
